match_phrases: your payouts are temporarily on hold
cause: Payments/Risk paused transfers while it verifies identity, bank details, or recent disputes. Checkout can stay live.
explanation: Forums consistently show this yellow/red admin banner with little detail. Official docs say: read the homepage banner and have the store owner check email. Community staff cannot see the hold reason.
steps: Read the exact banner on Home or Settings → Payments — it names verify, bank, chargeback, or review.
Sign in as the store owner. Staff often cannot open Complete account setup.
Check the owner inbox and spam for legal-mailer.shopify.com or Shopify Payments.
If the banner has Complete account setup or View documents, click that button (arrow).
If it only says wait / standard review, reply on the existing ticket — do not open a new chat.
done_if: payouts are no longer on hold
sources_note: Forums: merchants notice £0 next payout and a silent hold. Sidekick cannot lift Risk holds. Generic AIs invent “Settings → Bank” paths.

match_phrases: this store is currently unable to accept payments
cause: No active primary card provider. PayPal or Shop Pay alone does not satisfy this banner.
explanation: Official help uses this exact sentence. It is a setup gap, not a customer-card decline.
steps: Open Settings → Payments and look for a red/yellow setup banner.
If Shopify Payments is offered, click Complete account setup.
Otherwise Choose third-party provider and add a live card gateway.
Confirm status is Active (not Test, Draft, or Incomplete).
Incognito checkout: a real card method must appear under Pay.
sources_note: Docs are precise here. ChatGPT often suggests PayPal as the fix — that will not clear this banner.

match_phrases: your payment gateway was in test mode
cause: Provider is accepting only test cards. Live customers are declined; some orders stay stamped “created in test mode”.
explanation: Community threads show the banner toggle is not enough — you must Settings → Payments → Manage → uncheck Test mode → Save. Abandoned-cart links created in test mode can keep failing.
steps: Ignore the homepage teaser if it stays “on” — open Settings → Payments.
Click Manage on the card provider.
Uncheck Test mode. Save.
If a third-party gateway, swap sandbox API keys for live keys.
Send a fresh checkout link. Do not reuse a test-mode abandoned checkout.
sources_note: Forum accepted solution: Manage → Test mode, then a brand-new checkout. Sidekick sometimes toggles the wrong provider.

cause: The gateway returned a decline. One toast is a customer-bank issue; a store-wide toast storm is test mode, keys, or fraud rules.
explanation: Toasts vanish quickly. Capture them. Timeline on the order/abandoned checkout has the real code (generic_error, test_mode_live_card, config_error).
steps: If you still see the toast, note the exact words before it disappears.
Open the order or abandoned checkout → Timeline and copy the decline code.
test_mode_live_card → turn test mode off (see Test mode playbook).
config_error / invalid credentials → replace live API keys.
One customer, do_not_honor / insufficient_funds → ask them to retry or use Shop Pay.
sources_note: Gemini is decent if you screenshot the toast. ChatGPT without the code guesses fraud. Storescope keeps the toast text even after it fades.

cause: Inline Polaris validation — the form will not save. Usually a checksum fail or legal-name mismatch, not a hold yet.
explanation: Validation sits under the field in red, not in the top banner. OCR often misses it unless we scan the form body.
steps: Find the red helper text under the bank fields — that is the only source of truth.
Paste numbers from a statement. Drop spaces and hyphens.
Canadian transit is 5 digits + 3-digit institution; US routing is 9 digits.
Account holder must match the legal business name on Shopify Payments.
Save. If it saves but later says Needs attention, treat it as a bank-mismatch hold.

match_phrases: there are no shipping rates available
no shipping rates available for this address
cause: Checkout asked every matching profile and got zero rates — missing zone, weight, carrier disconnect, or an app that returned nothing.
explanation: Official troubleshooting starts with a draft order using the customer city/postal. Carrier apps (EasyShip, Zapiet, Addition) fail silently when the product has no weight or the location is not an origin.
steps: Reproduce with a draft order using the customer’s city, country, and postal code.
Settings → Shipping and delivery → Manage rates.
Put that country in exactly one zone that has at least one rate.
Add a fallback flat rate so a carrier API failure cannot zero out checkout.
Confirm every physical product has a weight and the inventory location is a shipping origin.
sources_note: Forums push carrier apps; docs push zones + fallback rate. Sidekick cannot see the customer’s postal code unless you paste it.

cause: The carrier account token expired or the plan does not include carrier-calculated rates.
explanation: CCS is plan-gated (Advanced/Plus, or an add-on). A disconnected badge next to Canada Post / UPS / USPS is the tell.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → Carrier accounts.
Reconnect the carrier and complete any OAuth.
If CCS is not on your plan, add a flat rate immediately so checkout lives.
Confirm the carrier is added inside the zone that covers the customer.
Retest with a new postal code so Shopify does not reuse a cached empty quote.

cause: Liquid failed to compile — unclosed tag, bad character, or an app embed writing into a section.
explanation: Duplicate the theme first. The file path in the red line (sections/header.liquid) is the jump target. App embeds frequently masquerade as theme bugs.
steps: Online Store → Themes → duplicate the live theme before touching code.
Click the red “Theme has N errors” banner or Edit code.
Open the file named in the error (often sections/header.liquid).
Fix the unclosed tag or revert that file from the version dropdown.
If the error appeared after an app install, disable that app embed and re-preview.
sources_note: Forums: always duplicate first. Sidekick can draft Liquid but merchants report it breaking sections. Generic AIs invent filters.

cause: The signed-in staff role lacks this resource. Not a store outage.
explanation: Payments, billing, and legal banners are often owner-only. Retry as owner or grant Finance / Settings.
steps: Note which button produced the toast (Save, View payouts, Billing).
Settings → Users and permissions → your user → check Finance, Settings, Apps.
Have the store owner open the same page — if the CTA appears, it is a permission gap.
Owner grants the permission or performs the step.
Re-scan. The toast should be gone and the banner CTA clickable.

cause: The location you are fulfilling from has no available units (on hand minus committed).
explanation: Available is not On hand. Transfers, drafts, and other locations hide stock.
steps: Open the product → Inventory and read Available at the fulfillment location.
If stock is at another location, fulfill from there or transfer.
Turn on Continue selling when out of stock only if you accept oversell.
Check apps that reserve inventory (preorder, bundles) — they reduce Available.
Retry fulfill. The red toast should clear.

match_phrases: payment failed for your shopify invoice
cause: Shopify could not charge the card on file for the plan or an app. Different from customer payouts.
explanation: A frozen store is almost always Settings → Billing, not Payments.
steps: Settings → Billing as the store owner.
Update the card and pay the open invoice.
Wait a few minutes if the store was frozen.
Check for a separate failed app charge.
Place a test order after it is current.

cause: DNS does not match Shopify’s expected A/CNAME, so SSL will not issue.
explanation: Extra AAAA or old CNAMEs are the usual stall.
steps: Online Store → Domains → the domain with the error.
Shopify-hosted: Verify connection and wait up to 24h.
Third-party: A → 23.227.38.65 and www CNAME → shops.myshopify.com.
Remove leftover AAAA / old CNAMEs.
Set it as primary once Connected so SSL can finish.

cause: A third-party embed, checkout UI extension, or outdated app is overriding native UI.
explanation: Shopify rarely names the app. Cleanest test: preview a clean theme, then disable embeds one by one.
steps: Note when it started (new app, theme publish, Shopify update).
Online Store → Themes → Customize → App embeds — disable the newest embed.
Settings → Apps — check for “Update” or unsupported checkout flags.
Preview Dawn (or a duplicate with embeds off) and retest the flow.
If the preview is clean, the embed is the culprit — leave it off or update the app.
sources_note: Sidekick cannot query whether an embed is actually live. Forums: disable newest app first.

cause: Often oversized cookies/headers or a broken app iframe — sometimes a Shopify status incident.
explanation: Dev forum staff: clear cookies first. Then status.shopify.com. Then try incognito as owner.
steps: Open status.shopify.com in another tab.
Hard-refresh. If every admin page errors, try incognito.
Clear cookies for admin.shopify.com and retry.
Disable recently installed admin apps / browser extensions.
If only one resource errors, duplicate the theme or uninstall that app.

cause: Validation, permission, or a network blip. The red field text (if any) wins over the toast.
explanation: If a field is red, it is validation. If the whole page toasts, check permission and network.
steps: Scroll the form for red helper text and fix that field.
If nothing is red, retry once — transient network toasts happen.
If it repeats, try owner + incognito (permission / extension).
Theme code saves: check the Liquid error banner instead.
Still failing: copy the toast into Ask and re-scan.

cause: Preferences still have the storefront password on. Checkout and Shop Pay checks can fail for outsiders.
explanation: A paid plan is required to remove the password. Friends hitting the password page is not a payments bug.
steps: Online Store → Preferences.
Turn off Restrict access to visitors with the password. Save.
If the toggle is locked, pick a paid plan first.
Open the storefront incognito — you should not see the password gate.
Retest Shop Pay / wallets; they often break while the password is on.
